featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst Biryani Ever – Avoid at All Costs
Don't fall for good review
I ordered biryani from on December 31st for my daughter's birthday party, and it was an absolute disaster. The biryani was horrific—the rice was uncooked, the taste was revolting, and it was obvious that the food was prepared by amateurs with zero culinary skills.

The food quality was so bad that none of my guests could eat it. To make matters worse, they promised to refund my money after I complained, but even after 4 days, I have received nothing. Adding to the frustration, they haven’t even bothered to collect their pot back.

This place is the epitome of unprofessionalism and irresponsibility. They ruined my event and caused unnecessary stress. Avoid them at all costs if you care about your sanity and reputation!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello Mr. Yadav,

We always appreciate feedback but prefer it to be fair and constructive. Let’s set the record straight with complete transparency:

We have reviewed your profile and seen your feedback about Barbeque Nation, where it seems the food didn't meet your expectations, along with a few other outlets. Given that, we may not place much weight on your average review. We, on the other hand, personally visit these places, and while we are in the same business, we genuinely appreciate their food. If your experiences don’t align, perhaps you should consider dining at Michelin-starred establishments.

1. The Root Cause: The issue with the rice occurred because it was freshly harvested from a new batch we specifically opened for your order. While fresh rice can sometimes result in slight texture variations, we tested the same batch with other team members, and they did not find it as disappointing as you have described.

2. Sample Approved: You picked up the sample beforehand, tasted it, and gave your approval. This makes your sudden dissatisfaction puzzling, especially since the same preparation process was followed for the final order.

3. Respectful Refund: The moment you provided feedback, we didn’t hesitate to offer a refund, despite the fact that your tone escalated with threats of a negative review. We respect every customer, even under such circumstances.

4. Price vs. Expectations: For ₹600/kg  Paneer Biryani (a price you negotiated from ₹600/kg and tried reducing to ₹550/kg), you seemed to expect gourmet-level biryani worthy of a five-star chef. To put this in perspective, high-end chefs charge significantly more, especially for large orders.

5. Pot: Asking us to collect the pot with leftovers still inside is unprofessional. Returning it clean, as is standard practice, would have been a simple gesture of mutual respect. Since we provide takeaways and delivery as a token of respect, and you came to collect a sample, I hope you understand. I agree where we are lagging, but be an effective communicator and then expect the same in return.

PS: You don’t need to disrespect the food, and as we mentioned during the call, you can recycle the pot. We will initiate your return as you have paid half payment ₹1500, but only once the pot is returned cleaned, since we didn’t promise delivery. If we are making this adjustment as a token of respect, we expect to be treated the same way.

We take pride in treating all customers professionally and upholding quality in our work. However, exaggerations and one-sided stories do not align with the mutual respect that makes association meaningful.

🌟 5/5 Stars – A Truly Soul-Satisfying Meal at Hotel Ekta Kathiyawadi! 🌟

We ordered Misal Pav, Kathiyawadi Thali, Dal Khichadi, French Fries, Jalebi, and Coffee — and every single dish was perfectly prepared, bursting with taste and freshness. The Kathiyawadi Thali stood out with its rich, rustic flavors, and the Dal Khichadi was pure comfort in a bowl. The crispy French Fries and piping hot Misal Pav added a lovely variety to our spread.

But what truly stole the show was the platter of chutneys and pickles served alongside — hands down, the best I’ve ever tasted! Each chutney had its own unique character, and the pickles were simply divine.

To end on a sweet note, the Jalebi was golden, crisp, and perfectly soaked, paired beautifully with a refreshing cup of coffee.

If you love food that speaks to your soul, Hotel Ekta Kathiyawadi is a must-visit. Delicious food, warm hospitality, and unbeatable flavors — it’s a five-star experience all the way! 🌶️🍛☕🍴

The Sev Tameta, Ringan no Olo, and Lasaniya Bataka were outstanding. The rotlas were served fresh with white butter and jaggery, which gave a proper village-style touch. The buttermilk was refreshing and perfectly balanced.
The ambience is simple yet traditional, giving proper Kathiyawadi dhaba vibes. Service was quick, polite, and very attentive. Portions are generous and pricing is reasonable considering the quality and taste.
If you love spicy, desi, authentic Kathiyawadi food, this place is a must-visit. Definitely coming back again!

However, while the ambiance was great, we were a bit disappointed with the food. For the price, we anticipated something more flavorful and well-prepared. The high cost of the dish felt a bit steep compared to the portion and taste we received.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mood for some गावठी Dhaba food!
.
A few days ago I along with my bunch of loved ones decided to visit Aryan Agri Katta. It’s a dhaba which is located at NH 48. The place is simple but spacious. They also have hut style seating areas where a group of 10- 15 people can have their dinner.
.
We started by ordering some appetizers.
.
Masala Papad
A perfect munching option while you are deciding on the menu.
Crisp and delicious papad topped with onions, tomatoes, some spices and sev.
.
Chicken Lollipop
Being favourite and specially loved by kids we ordered chicken lollipop.
They were perfectly cooked, perfect crisp and immensely appetizing.
.
Chicken Tandoori
We had ordered 3 different types of tandoori: Normal, White & Schezwan.
All 3 were great and had its own taste but personally, I liked Schezwan tandoori.
.
They have a live chicken counter and for our dinner, we picked 2 live chicken from it. 1 was Gavthi Chicken & other was Kadaknath Chicken.
.
Gavthi Chicken
It’s always said that having Ghar ka khana is better than having restaurant food; same goes with chicken. Having gavthi chicken over broiler is always good.
The chicken curry was spicy and perfectly made by adding spices. The chicken was tender and tasted nice.
.
Kadaknath Chicken
It’s a chicken which is completely black and is known for its high iron content and much lower cholesterol than other breeds and sells at a much higher price than other varieties.
The chicken curry was spicy and perfectly made by adding spices. The chicken was tender and tasted nice. just superb. It was made in Agri style and I liked Kadaknath chicken curry over Gavthi chicken curry.
The chicken was cooked perfectly but at the same time I couldn’t eat the pieces more maybe because of its blackish-grey colour but I thoroughly enjoyed the gravy.
.

featured_reviews.name: Sweta Tandel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I remember when this restaurant first opened; the food was truly authentic, packed with traditional flavors, and every dish felt like a careful, home-cooked labor of love. It was a local gem, and I recommended it to everyone. Unfortunately, based on our experience today, something fundamental in the kitchen has changed, and the taste is no longer the same.
​We visited today hoping for that original, rich experience, but were severely let down by both main components of our order.
​First, the bhakri we received was undoubtedly stale. It was tough, brittle, and tasted distinctly like it had been prepared yesterday and merely reheated.
​Second, the mutton gravy was the biggest disappointment in terms of flavor. The texture and profile felt altered, and upon closer inspection, it was clear why: the dish was bulked up with large amounts of capsicum (bell peppers). While capsicum is a great vegetable, it has absolutely no place in a traditional mutton preparation and completely overrides the authentic spices and meat flavor. This seems like a cost-cutting measure to increase the volume of the dish, but it has killed the signature taste that made this place great.
